data.title: Suvarnabhumi airport ends free parking for flooded motorists
data.description: Suvarnabhumi airport has advised car owners with flooded homes who parked their vehicles there to remove them immediately, or start paying.

data.title: Top court accepts NBTC chief's appeal
data.description: The Supreme Administrative Court has agreed to rule on an appeal by National Broadcasting and Telecommunications Commission (NBTC) chairman Sarana Boonbaichaiyapruck in a dispute over his eligibility to hold the post.

data.title: Justice minister unaware of details of Thaksin’s amnesty request
data.description: Justice Minister Rutthapon Naowarat said on Tuesday he was unaware of the details of former prime minister Thaksin Shinawatra’s petition seeking an amnesty under the Peaceful Society Promotion Act, and would not be involved.

data.title: No drugs, violence evident in vlogger Hlun Solo's death
data.description: Investigators in Georgia say they have so far found no trace of dangerous substances or evidence suggesting violence in the death of popular Thai travel vlogger Hlun Solo in the capital, Tbilisi, in July.

data.title: Eight districts remain flooded as drainage efforts continue
data.description: Floodwaters have receded in parts of Bangkok, leaving eight districts still affected as authorities continue drainage and cleanup operations.

data.title: Varawut  vows action  over leaks
data.description: Industry Minister Varawut Silpa-archa has pledged strict inspections and immediate closure orders for factories breaking the law following a chemical leak from industrial waste in Prachin Buri that, compounded by flooding, has caused damage and hardship for residents.

data.title: PM confident  of coalition bloc's unity
data.description: Prime Minister and Interior Minister Anutin Charnvirakul yesterday expressed confidence that the ruling coalition would remain united during the upcoming no-confidence debate, saying he trusted coalition partner Pheu Thai to stand by Bhumjaithai (BJT).

data.title: Act now to avoid next 'great repression', IMF says
data.description: Reforms to boost growth, alongside credible tax and spending plans, could help governments avoid a new wave of financial repression, an International Monetary Fund (IMF) official said on Monday.

data.title: Anutin courts Japanese EV manufacturers
data.description: Prime Minister Anutin Charnvirakul has invited Japanese automakers to use Thailand as an electric vehicle (EV) production base, pledging to protect the existing automotive industry.

data.title: Youth leaders leave for China
data.description: A delegation of 40 Thai youths is visiting China's Yunnan province for a 13-day study programme focusing on ethnic cultures, agriculture, community-based tourism and cooperation in the Mekong subregion.

data.title: Heavy rain alert  for flooded areas
data.description: The government's Joint Information Centre on Monday urged people in flood-prone areas to monitor conditions closely, with heavy rain forecast in parts of the country from Oct 13-18.

data.title: Designers showcase Thai silk
data.description: Designers from more than 100 countries are showcasing creations made with Thai silk in Bangkok as Thailand hosts the 2026 annual meetings of the International Monetary Fund (IMF) and World Bank Group.

data.title: Air force sets out roadmap  for upgrades
data.description: Royal Thai Air Force (RTAF) commander ACM Seksan Kantha has unveiled a 2027-2028 roadmap to strengthen the force's capabilities and safeguard Thailand's airspace and sovereignty under the vision of an "Unbeatable Air Force".

data.title: Thailand has become 'the sick man of Asia': Korn
data.description: Democrat Party deputy leader Korn Chatikavanij warned that Thailand risks falling into an economic trap, saying the country has gone from being an economic success story to the "sick man of Asia".

data.title: Ekniti pushes AI for all
data.description: Better jobs, stronger skills and broader access to the benefits of AI are Thailand's key priorities as the technology transforms work and business, Deputy Prime Minister and Finance Minister Ekniti Nitithanprapas said.

data.title: 10,000 tonnes of flood-trash cleared from Bangkok streets
data.description: The Bangkok Metropolitan Administration (BMA) has already collected more than 10,000 tonnes of post-flood garbage as the water retreats across the capital, with a "Buddy District" task force accelerating recovery efforts.

data.title: Call for adventure tourism accountability after 2 tourists injured
data.description: PHETCHABUN - Phetchabun authorities face calls to review adventure tourism safety rules and compliance after two foreigners were injured in a fall from a cliff while abseiling over the weekend.

data.title: Korean wanted for child porn distribution arrested in Bangkok
data.description: Police were able to find and detain a 42-year-old South Korean man at a condominium in Bangkok wanted in his home country for allegedly distributing pornographic videos of teenage girls online.

data.title: Koh Samui villa hit by landslide
data.description: SURAT THANI: A villa on Koh Samui was reported hit by landslide on Monday with local administrators warning of more due to rain-soaked soil.

data.title: Progressive team takes control of Social Security Board
data.description: The Progressive Social Security team has taken control of the Social Security Office Board with a dominating win over their rivals in Sunday's election.

data.title: Delays on Bangkok's Blue Line service
data.description: Trains running on the MRT's Blue Line were experiencing delays of up to 10 minutes on Monday due to a "technical disruption".

data.title: Flooding continues in Bangkok and 20 provinces
data.description: The Department of Disaster Prevention and Mitigation reported on Monday that flooding continues to make life wretched for people in parts of Bangkok and 20 provinces, mostly in the Central Plains.

data.title: Heavy rain may return to Greater Bangkok on Tuesday
data.description: The Meteorological Department predicts heavy rain will be in the South on Monday and expand to the lower North, the lower Northeast, the Central Plains including Greater Bangkok and the East on Tuesday.

data.title: Protest ban near IMF venues
data.description: The Metropolitan Police Bureau (MPB) has banned public gatherings around the Queen Sirikit National Convention Center (QSNCC), venues hosting official functions and hotels accommodating delegates to the IMF-World Bank Annual Meetings 2026 until Oct 20.

data.title: Retirement scheme near finish
data.description: An early retirement scheme for civil servants is nearing completion, with plans to reduce the civil service workforce by 5% annually, starting in fiscal 2027, says Deputy Prime Minister for Legal Affairs Pakorn Nilprapunt.

data.title: JIC denies delaying new talks
data.description: Thailand has denied Cambodia's claim that it is delaying a Joint Boundary Commission (JBC) meeting and hindering border surveys and demarcation.

data.title: Poverty falls, but 3.6m remain at risk
data.description: Thailand's poverty rate fell to 3.27% in 2025, leaving 2.3 million people below the poverty line. But another 3.6 million remain at risk of joining them if their incomes take a hit, the National Economic and Social Development Council (NESDC) said.

data.title: DDC: No plague outbreak in Russia
data.description: The Department of Disease Control (DDC) said on Sunday there was no evidence of an outbreak in Russia following reports of a suspected death from pneumonic plague there.
